entries.text: When the "put" action fails to place an object on a surface or in a receptacle, try the alternative phrasing "move <object> to <target>" as it often succeeds.
Before placing an object into a closed receptacle (e.g., microwave, fridge), open it first; if "put" still fails after opening, switch to "move <object> to <receptacle>".
Systematically search likely locations for the target object (countertops, diningtable, fridge, cabinets, drawers, shelves) one by one, and once found, take it before proceeding to the cooling step.
To cool an object, go to the fridge and use "cool <object> with fridge 1" even if the fridge is closed—this action works without needing to open it first.

When a "put" action repeatedly fails despite the receptacle being open and the object being in inventory, do not waste turns retrying the same phrasing or re-opening/re-closing the receptacle; immediately switch to "move <object> to <receptacle>" to complete the placement.
